content: Fatty acid desaturase 2 (FADS2) is a gene that encodes the enzyme known as Delta-6 desaturase (D6D). Although the enzyme is primarily referred to as D6D, it has also been shown to catalyze reactions involving delta-8 and delta-4 desaturases, despite the naming conventions. FADS2 belongs to the fatty acid desaturase (FADS) gene family. Enzymes in this family are responsible for introducing double bonds into fatty acid chains, a process known as desaturation. Members of the FADS family are considered to be fusion proteins, consisting of two main domains: an N-terminal cytochrome b5-like domain and a C-terminal desaturase domain that spans multiple membranes. Both domains are characterized by conserved histidine motifs, which are critical for their enzymatic activity. The FADS2 gene is located on chromosome 11 at the 11q12-q13.1 region, where it is clustered with other family members, FADS1 and FADS3. This clustering is believed to have arisen through evolutionary gene duplication, as evidenced by the similar exon/intron structures of these genes. In terms of clinical significance, FADS2 has been studied for its potential role in cognitive development. One study suggested that breastfed children carrying the C allele of the FADS2 gene scored approximately 7 IQ points higher than those with the less common G allele, although this difference was reduced when maternal IQ was taken into account. However, a subsequent replication attempt involving 5,934 eight-year-old children failed to confirm these findings. In this larger study, no association was found between the common C allele and any negative effects of formula feeding. Contrary to the original report, children who were homozygous for the rare GG genotype performed worse when formula-fed compared to other formula-fed children. Additionally, a more recent study involving over 700 families found no evidence to support either a direct effect or a moderating effect of the original single nucleotide polymorphism (SNP) (rs174575) on offspring IQ. Furthermore, no significant effects were observed for two other FADS2 polymorphisms (rs1535 and rs174583), nor was there any influence of maternal FADS2 genotype on the IQ of their children.
